# Mohammad Arif

> Product security engineer, security researcher and DEF CON speaker with 5+ years across application security, cloud security, DevSecOps and AI security. This site hosts my security write-ups and study notes.

## Main pages
- [Homepage](https://mohdarif.com/): background, experience, projects, talks and contact
- [All notes and writing](https://mohdarif.com/notes/): index of every write-up

## Featured write-ups
- [JWT Security: Attacks and Server-Side Validation](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/jwt-security.html): How JWT attacks work (alg, kid, jku, jwk, weak secrets, claim and authorization flaws) and how to prevent each one with server-side validation.
- [Kubernetes Series, Part 1: How Kubernetes Works](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/k8s-part-1-introduction.html): Part 1 of a Kubernetes security series: cluster architecture, how a request flows, and the core objects, with diagrams.
- [Kubernetes Series, Part 2: Supply Chain Security](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/k8s-part-2-supply-chain.html): Part 2 of a Kubernetes security series: check what goes into your images and manifests with Syft, Grype, Trivy, kube-linter and kubesec, and choose a registry safely.
- [Kubernetes Series, Part 3: Monitoring, Logging and Runtime Security](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/k8s-part-3-monitoring-runtime.html): Part 3 of a Kubernetes security series: what to log and watch, how to detect attacks inside running containers with Falco, and what to do when a Pod is compromised.
- [OWASP Kubernetes Top 10 (2025): A Practical Guide](https://mohdarif.com/notes/kubernetes/owasp-k8s-top-10.html): The OWASP Kubernetes Top 10 (2025) explained simply: what each risk is, a command to check for it, and how to fix it.
- [Threat Modeling a Multi-Tenant AI Document Platform](https://mohdarif.com/notes/LLM/threat-model-ai-document-platform.html): A worked threat model for a multi-tenant AI document analysis platform on AWS: trust boundaries, attack paths, controls, launch priorities and how to test them.
- [Investigating and Containing Compromised AWS STS Credentials Across Accounts](https://mohdarif.com/notes/aws-security/cross-account-sts-incident-response.html): A worked AWS incident response: trace a bulk S3 download to an STS session using only one account's CloudTrail, then contain it without taking down the services that share the role.
- [SSRF on AWS: From a URL Parameter to Instance Credentials](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/ssrf-aws-metadata-credentials.html): How an image-download feature on EC2 can leak AWS credentials, why three common fixes fail, and what a safe design looks like.
- [Broken Access Control in a Document API: From IDOR to Enterprise Sharing](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/broken-access-control-idor.html): Why a valid JWT is not enough to read a document, why checking the tenant is not enough either, and how to design and test object-level authorization.
- [SQL Injection in Practice: Values, Column Names, Stored Data and Stored Procedures](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/sql-injection-values-identifiers.html): SQL injection beyond the basics: why placeholders work for values but not column names, how second-order injection works, and why stored procedures are not automatically safe.
- [Insecure Deserialization in Python: Why pickle.loads() on Untrusted Data Is Code Execution](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/insecure-deserialization-python-pickle.html): How Python pickle runs code while loading data, why checks after pickle.loads() come too late, why authenticated senders are not trusted senders, how it differs from Java and PHP deserialization, and how to fix or contain it.
- [S3 Presigned URLs: Why Revoking Access Doesn't Stop the Download](https://mohdarif.com/notes/aws-security/s3-presigned-url-revocation.html): Why a presigned S3 URL keeps working after you revoke a user's access, how to contain one document right now, and how to design for fast, per-user revocation.

## AI and LLM notes
- [How LLM Systems Work, With Security Risks and Controls at Every Layer](https://mohdarif.com/notes/LLM/llm-security-starter.html): How modern LLM systems work layer by layer, what can go wrong at each layer, and which security controls reduce the risk.
- [Attention Is All You Need: Beginner Guide to Transformer Attention](https://mohdarif.com/notes/LLM/attention_is_all_you_need.html): Visual beginner notes on the Transformer paper: embeddings, positional encoding, self-attention, multi-head attention, the encoder and decoder, and the full Transformer flow.
- [OpenAI Prompting and Embeddings: Beginner Guide](https://mohdarif.com/notes/LLM/openai_prompting_embeddings.html): Beginner notes on prompting (a good prompt formula, few-shot examples, output control) and on text embeddings (similar meaning is closer in vector space, and how embeddings power search and RAG).

## AI agent security: prompt injection through GitHub and MCP (a four-page scenario)
These four pages walk through one scenario: an AI agent connected to GitHub through MCP (Model Context Protocol) reads a malicious public issue and leaks private repository code.
- [GitHub AI Agent Security: Prompt Injection in Dev Workflows](https://mohdarif.com/notes/MCP/github_mcp_issue.html): Overview and entry point: how prompt injection can lead an AI agent with repository access to expose private code, and which design choices make such a system vulnerable or secure.
- [GitHub AI Agent Attack Flow: Public Issue to Private Code](https://mohdarif.com/notes/MCP/attack-flow.html): The attack step by step: the attacker plants hidden instructions in a public issue, the victim asks the agent an ordinary question, and the agent follows the hidden instructions and posts private code.
- [GitHub AI Agent Vulnerability: Security Risks and Impact](https://mohdarif.com/notes/MCP/risk-impact.html): The impact of the scenario: private code exposure, business data theft, credential compromise, loss of trust, supply chain attacks, compliance violations and how the attack scales.
- [Exploitable vs Non-Exploitable: GitHub AI Agent Issue](https://mohdarif.com/notes/MCP/security-comparison.html): The conditions that make the scenario exploitable (public issues as untrusted input, MCP access without sanitization, "Always Allow" tool mode, cross-repository access) and the controls that make it non-exploitable.

## Web security interactive notes
- [OAuth 2.0 and OIDC Threat Model: Where Login Flows Break](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/OAuth-threat_model.html): An interactive threat model that maps OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect authorization bugs to the lifecycle stage where each control belongs.
- [PKCE Explained Interactively: Stopping Authorization Code Theft](https://mohdarif.com/notes/web-security/PKCE.html): How the OAuth PKCE extension stops a stolen authorization code from being redeemed by an attacker, explained interactively.

## AWS Certified Security Specialty (SCS-C03) study guides
- [AWS Security Specialty (SCS-C03) Domain 1: Detection](https://mohdarif.com/notes/aws-security/detection.html): A visual study sheet for Domain 1 (Detection): GuardDuty, Security Hub, Detective, CloudTrail and Insights, EventBridge, CloudWatch, Macie, Inspector, VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 Resolver query logs and Athena, with exam traps and quick-recall workflows.
- [Amazon GuardDuty Study Guide for the AWS Security Specialty](https://mohdarif.com/notes/aws-security/detection/guardduty_study_guide.html): An interactive study guide to Amazon GuardDuty: what it sees, what each protection plan adds, how finding severity works, and Extended Threat Detection.
- [AWS Security Hub Study Guide (SCS-C03)](https://mohdarif.com/notes/aws-security/detection/securityhub-study-guide.html): A study guide to AWS Security Hub: architecture, the ASFF finding format, workflow status and severity, compliance standards and the security score, cross-Region aggregation, automation, integrations, pricing and limits, with the top 10 exam traps and flashcards.

## Other
- [Python 3.11 Data Structures and Algorithms Cheat Sheet](https://mohdarif.com/notes/python_cheatsheet.html): An interactive Python 3.11 cheat sheet for the syntax used in data structures and algorithms: lists, strings, dictionaries and sets, deques, heaps and pattern matching, with time complexity notes.
